about: What scripts/content (the content standard, scripts/content/standard.json) needs to know about this site: where the documentation pages are, one persona per stakeholder of app/src/Architecture.lex.tex (the gate refuses a stakeholder without one), which persona guides which page, and the terms only this site uses. The same five guides appear on every Prism model's site, so a reader meets the same characters wherever they go.

personas.name: Kai
personas.need: A working Prism model of my own Cargo workspace, without writing it by hand.

asks.discover: What is Prism, and what would it do for my Rust code?
asks.evaluate: Will it read my workspace as it is, or make me rewrite it?
asks.learn: Show me each command and what it writes.
asks.build: How do I make an app that does what I need?
asks.scale: How do I keep my model in step as my code changes?

personas.name: Iris
personas.need: To see how a complete model is laid out, one record kind at a time.

asks.discover: How is a complete Prism model laid out?
asks.evaluate: Is every record here traced back to its source?
asks.learn: Walk me through each facet, one record kind at a time.
asks.build: Which pattern fits the app I have in mind?
asks.scale: How do I ship it and keep it verified?

personas.name: Vera
personas.need: Evidence that what the model claims about threats and controls is true.

asks.discover: What does this system claim, and who checks it?
asks.evaluate: Which threats are modeled, and what answers each one?
asks.learn: Where does each control come from?
asks.build: Can a mistake here slip past the checks?
asks.scale: Is the release signed, and can I trace it?

personas.name: Wren
personas.need: To know which records no page teaches yet, and who each page is for.

asks.discover: Who is each page for, and what do they need first?
asks.evaluate: Which claims can I make, and which are proved?
asks.learn: Which records does no page teach yet?
asks.scale: How do the docs stay in step without hand edits?

personas.name: Otto
personas.need: Everything kept in step when the subject changes, with no generated page edited by hand.

asks.discover: What runs where, and who owns it?
asks.build: Where does a new rule or route go?
asks.scale: How do releases and re-pins happen on their own?

reading.tutorial: A tutorial: follow the steps in order. Each one works if the one before it did.
reading.howToGuide: A how-to guide: each section is one step toward one task. Skip what you already have.
reading.reference: Reference: look up what you need. Nothing here asks to be read in order.
reading.explanation: Explanation: read it end to end, away from the keyboard.
reading.home: Start here. Each card leads to the pages for one reader or one stage.

terms.plain: A table of rules, as in OMG DMN 1.5: each row says which inputs lead to which outcome.
OASIS eXtensible Access Control Markup Language 3.0: a policy decides permit, deny, not applicable or indeterminate.
A model of something that is always in one state and moves between states on events, as in UML 2.5.1.
The stages a developer goes through with a product: discover, evaluate, learn, build and scale (Lewko and Parton).
One JSON document that describes an app. The builder turns it into every facet of a Prism model.
